question: From which date, Indian Financial year begins?
solution:
The correct answer is __**1st April**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Indian Financial Year begins on **1st April** and ends on **31st March** of the next year.
 
• This accounting period is used by the Government of India and most businesses to prepare financial statements and reports.
 
• The financial year starting from 1st April aligns with the agricultural cycle in India, facilitating better planning and budgeting for the government and businesses.
 
• This timeline is also followed for the implementation of the government's fiscal policies and budgetary allocations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Financial Year**

 
 
• A financial year, also known as a fiscal year, is a period used for calculating annual financial statements in businesses and other organizations.
 
• In India, the financial year starts on 1st April and ends on 31st March of the following year.
 
• This period is used by the government for budgeting and by companies for financial reporting and tax assessment.
 
 
 
• **Budget**
 
 
• The budget is a financial plan for a defined period, often one year.
 
• It is used by governments and organizations to manage income and expenditure.
 
• The Union Budget of India, which is presented annually on 1st February, outlines the revenue and expenditure for the upcoming financial year starting from 1st April.
 
 
 
• **Accounting Period**
 
 
• An accounting period is a span of time at the end of which financial statements are prepared to measure the financial performance of an entity.
 
• In India, the standard accounting period is the financial year from 1st April to 31st March.
 
• This period ensures uniformity and consistency in financial reporting and tax assessment.
 
 
 
• **Fiscal Policies**
 
 
• Fiscal policies refer to the use of government spending and tax policies to influence economic conditions.
 
• These policies are planned and executed in alignment with the financial year to achieve economic goals like growth, employment, and inflation control.
 
• The financial year timeline helps in systematic planning and implementation of these policies.
